cond-auto-assess.scene: the patient sits on the edge of the treatment table, seen from behind; the practitioner stands at the patient's right side and rests only his RIGHT hand flat on the patient's upper back just beside the spine, fingertips pointing toward the neck, while his left arm hangs relaxed at his side; nothing else touches the patient, and no arm or hand enters the frame from the camera side or from any edge
cond-auto-assess.anat: the neck and upper back only: the seven neck vertebrae and the upper thoracic spine in one midline column, with the two shoulder blades on either side, seen from behind; nothing below the shoulder blades
cond-auto-assess.pain: the lowest neck vertebrae and the muscles between the shoulder blades
cond-auto-assess.guide: The shoulder blades sit on the UPPER back, one on each side of the spine, just below the shoulders. Draw only the structures named, not the whole skeleton.

cond-fibro-treat.scene: the camera stands at the foot end of the treatment table looking along the patient's back toward her head, so her spine runs straight up the middle of the frame: the patient lies face down with her face in the face cradle and a soft blanket over her hips and legs; the practitioner stands at the side of the table and holds a small chrome spring-loaded adjusting instrument shaped like a thick pen with a flat rubber tip (no needle) gently against the muscles beside her upper spine, his other hand resting flat on her back
cond-fibro-treat.anat: the upper and mid back only: the spine as one straight midline column running up the middle of the frame to the base of her neck, with the two shoulder blades on either side of it
cond-fibro-treat.pain: a few small scattered tender points on the muscles on either side of the upper spine
cond-fibro-treat.guide: Because the patient lies face down and the camera looks down at the back, the overlay is a BACK VIEW (posterior view) seen from above: the spine is a single straight column along the midline groove of the back, its row of spinous processes pointing up toward the skin and the camera, the vertebral bodies hidden beneath. The shoulder blades sit on the UPPER back, one on each side of the spine, just below the shoulders. Draw only the structures named, not the whole skeleton.

cond-lbp-assess.scene: the patient lies on his back on the treatment table, one leg raised straight to about 30 degrees; the practitioner's flat hand presses gently down just above that ankle while his other hand steadies the patient's hip; the camera is far enough back that the patient's whole body fits inside the frame with clear space beyond the top of his head and beyond his toes; natural adult proportions: the legs are longer than the torso
cond-lbp-assess.anat: the lumbar spine, the pelvis, and the thigh bone drawn inside the RAISED thigh
cond-lbp-assess.pain: the lower back and the hip flexor where it attaches to the lumbar spine
cond-lbp-assess.guide: Draw only the structures named, not the whole skeleton.

cond-osteo-treat.scene: the camera stands at the foot end of the treatment table looking along the patient's back toward her head, so her spine runs straight up the middle of the frame: the patient, a woman in her seventies with short silver hair, lies face down on a well-padded treatment table with a pillow under her chest and a light blanket over her hips and legs; the practitioner stands at the side of the table and holds a small chrome spring-loaded adjusting instrument shaped like a thick pen with a flat rubber tip (no needle) lightly against her mid back, his other hand resting still on her shoulder
cond-osteo-treat.anat: the mid back only: a short straight column of vertebrae running up the middle of her back, with the inner ends of a few ribs on either side
cond-osteo-treat.guide: Because the patient lies face down and the camera looks down at the back, the overlay is a BACK VIEW (posterior view) seen from above: the spine is a single straight column along the midline groove of the back, its row of spinous processes pointing up toward the skin and the camera, the vertebral bodies hidden beneath. Draw only the structures named, not the whole skeleton.

cond-plantar-treat.scene: a close side view of the patient's bare right foot and ankle resting on a folded white towel at the end of the treatment table, the inner arch of the foot facing the camera; only this one foot is in the frame, natural adult size; a white stand-mounted low-level laser head on an articulated arm, positioned a hand's width above the heel and projecting three thin red laser lines onto the skin without touching it
cond-plantar-treat.anat: a SIDE VIEW of the foot skeleton inside the foot: the heel bone (calcaneus) filling the heel, the ankle bone (talus) above it, the arch of the midfoot bones, the five long metatarsals and the toe bones running into the toes, and the plantar fascia as a band along the sole from the underside of the heel bone to the ball of the foot
cond-plantar-treat.pain: where the plantar fascia attaches to the underside of the heel bone
cond-plantar-treat.guide: Draw only the structures named, not the whole skeleton.
cond-plantar-treat.who: an adult; only the lower leg and the right foot are in frame

svc-fx635-device.scene: the white stand-mounted low-level laser on its single articulated arm fills the upper half of the frame, its head a hand's width above the patient's heel and projecting three thin red laser lines onto it without touching; below it, the patient's bare right foot and lower leg lie on a folded white towel at the end of the treatment table, seen from the side with the inner arch facing the camera; only this one foot is in the frame, natural adult size; the practitioner's hand rests on the laser arm
svc-fx635-device.anat: a SIDE VIEW of the foot skeleton inside the foot: the heel bone (calcaneus) filling the heel, the ankle bone (talus) above it, the arch of the midfoot bones, the five long metatarsals and the toe bones running into the toes, and the plantar fascia as a band along the sole from the underside of the heel bone to the ball of the foot
svc-fx635-device.pain: where the plantar fascia attaches to the underside of the heel bone
svc-fx635-device.guide: Draw only the structures named, not the whole skeleton.
svc-fx635-device.who: an adult; only the lower leg and the right foot are in frame

cond-neck-treat.scene: the camera stands at the foot end of the treatment table looking along the patient's back toward her head, so her spine runs straight up the middle of the frame: the patient lies face down with her face in the face cradle and a light blanket over her hips and legs; the practitioner stands at the side of the table with his two hands resting one over the other on her upper back between the shoulder blades
cond-neck-treat.anat: the upper back only: the upper thoracic spine in one midline column running up the middle of the frame to the base of her neck, and the two shoulder blades on either side of it, each with its broad top edge near the shoulder and its lower tip pointing down the back toward her feet
cond-neck-treat.pain: between the shoulder blades and the base of the neck
cond-neck-treat.guide: Because the patient lies face down and the camera looks down at the back, the overlay is a BACK VIEW (posterior view) seen from above: the spine is a single straight column along the midline groove of the back, its row of spinous processes pointing up toward the skin and the camera, the vertebral bodies hidden beneath. The shoulder blades sit on the UPPER back, one on each side of the spine, just below the shoulders. Draw only the structures named, not the whole skeleton.

cond-osteo-assess.scene: the patient, a woman in her seventies with short silver hair in a soft cardigan and slacks, stands on one foot beside the treatment table, seen from her left side: her left hand holds the edge of the table, and her right arm is on the far side of her body, out of view; the practitioner stands just behind her with both hands hovering close to her waist, ready to steady her
cond-osteo-assess.anat: the spine, the pelvis and the hip joints
cond-osteo-assess.pain: the mid back and the hip
cond-osteo-assess.guide: Draw only the structures named, not the whole skeleton.

cond-lbp-assess (round 3, second try).scene: a wide shot from further back: the patient lies on his back on the treatment table, one leg raised straight to about 30 degrees; the practitioner's flat hand presses gently down just above that ankle while his other hand steadies the patient's hip; the table and the patient sit in the middle of the frame, with the pillow, a strip of floor and clinic furniture clearly visible beyond the top of his head on one side and beyond his toes on the other, so his whole body including the back of his head and all his toes is well inside the frame; natural adult proportions: the legs are longer than the torso
cond-lbp-assess (round 3, second try).anat: the lumbar spine, the pelvis with the hip joint of the raised leg, and the thigh bone inside the raised thigh
cond-lbp-assess (round 3, second try).pain: the lower back and the hip flexor where it attaches to the lumbar spine
